name: Red vine leaf extract
short: Uncontrolled 6-week study (65 with venous insufficiency): 6 patients had possibly related adverse events, 4 gut problems. 12-week placebo trials: tolerability like placebo; rare, usually mild events.
text: The cited trials tested one coded red vine leaf extract taken by mouth in people with chronic venous insufficiency. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 248 patients, its tolerability was similar to that of placebo; in another 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 260 patients, adverse events were rare and usually mild, and the two serious adverse events (hospitalisations) and three further withdrawals for adverse events occurred with placebo. In a 6-week open observational study in 65 patients without a control group, six patients had adverse events potentially related to the extract, four of them gastrointestinal problems. A systematic review of 5 trials reported tolerability as good or satisfactory and called for further high-quality trials. The three individually cited studies lasted at most 12 weeks (the review abstract does not give trial durations), and the abstracts give no data on pregnancy or longer use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
